LESSON: PRESSURE

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: PHYSICS
Strand: Mechanics and Thermal Physics
Topic 1.2: Pressure
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 24

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Pressure, part of Mechanics and Thermal Physics in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 PHYSICS.

Key inquiry question: How does density of fluid, acceleration due to gravity and depth below the free surface affect pressure in fluid?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Discuss with peers the meaning of atmospheric pressure. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point /sign/write) during the discussion, 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Discuss with peers the meaning of atmospheric pressure. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication- AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to-speech application/ point /sign/write) during the discussion, 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Pressure together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and collaboration: as the learner develops speaking and listening skills when they are discussing the

applications of atmospheric pressure and transmission of pressure in fluids.

• Digital Literacy: as the learner acquires manipulation skills when they are using digital media to search for more

information on the applications of atmospheric pressure and transmission of pressure in fluids.

Values

● Love: as the learner practices the virtue of sharing when they use available resources and avoid inflicting pain on

others while carrying out activities to demonstrate the existence of atmospheric pressure in nature.

● Respect: as the learner acquires skills in respecting diverse opinions as they discuss the transmission of pressure in

fluid.

Environmental Issues:

• Climate change: the learner relates the effect of atmospheric pressure to climate change as they discuss the
